findings: src/execution/physical_plan/plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate: the bit check becomes `perfect_hash_bits > MaxValue(PerfectHtThresholdSetting, 18)`, and the later size check accepts any table of up to 4MB. So `perfect_ht_threshold` no longer limits or disables perfect hashing; it only adds to the built-in 18-bit/4MB allowance. A user who sets `PRAGMA perfect_ht_threshold=0` (the documented way to turn it off, and the workaround for corrupt statistics that triggers the 'exceeded total groups' exception) still gets PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY for every key that fits in 18 bits/4MB.

Concrete break: test/optimizer/perfect_ht.test lines 17-33 set perfect_ht_threshold=0 and then 1, and expect the plan for `SELECT year, SUM(val), COUNT(val), COUNT(*) FROM timeseries GROUP BY year` NOT to contain PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY. With this patch the year key (a few bits, tiny state) passes the 4MB check, so these assertions should fail. test/sql/filter/test_filter_clause.test_slow:428 also relies on threshold=0 to force the regular hash path. This overrides what the user configured.

The lazy-initialisation part of perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp looks correct. AddChunk flags each group before initialising it, so a group repeated in one chunk is initialised once; the error path initialises the slots already flagged; Combine initialises new target slots before combining them; Destroy and Scan visit only set slots; NextSetGroup handles the tail of the flag array when its length is not a multiple of 8. I see no correctness issue in this file.
required_changes: Keep perfect_ht_threshold as a strict upper bound that the user controls. Either add the 18-bit/4MB extension only when the user has not changed the setting (it is at its default), or never let the extension go above an explicitly configured value. In both cases perfect_ht_threshold=0 or 1 must still disable perfect hashing as test/optimizer/perfect_ht.test expects.
Run test/optimizer/perfect_ht.test, test/sql/aggregate/aggregates/test_perfect_ht.test and test/sql/filter/test_filter_clause.test_slow and confirm they pass unmodified.
